title: Produce a compatibility-researched VCF 9.0 workload-domain architecture
prompt:
Produce the deployment architecture, not a prose architecture review. Implement exactly one new source file, `VcfArchitecture.java`, in the default package. Use only the Java 17 standard library and do not add build files, dependencies, generated sources, or any other implementation file. The protected `TestMain.java` harness constructs `new VcfArchitecture()` and calls `String design(Path estateInventory, Path compatibilitySnapshot)`. Return one JSON architecture document; do not write to the fixture files.

Read `fixtures/estate-inventory.json` for the existing fleet and the requested greenfield workload domain. The existing management domain is already on 9.0 and must not be changed. Design the requested workload domain as a new VCF 9.0 domain in that fleet, meeting the stated capacity after loss of either data site, preserving the requested two-data-site plus witness-site placement, and using the host, DNS, VLAN, vDS, vSAN ESA, vCenter, and dedicated NSX values supplied by the fixture. A secret-reference string in the fixture is intentional architecture data; preserve it exactly rather than inventing a credential.

Before implementing, use the harness's genuine network access to research current, real, reachable Broadcom-published compatibility, interoperability, and upgrade-path material relevant to VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 and the component versions in the estate. Consult fetched source pages, not only search-result snippets. You choose the searches and sources: no particular query or URL is prescribed. In the returned document add `researchConsulted`, an array with required string fields `title`, `url`, `accessDate`, and `finding` for each source page; use the exact absolute source URL, an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` access date, and a concise finding. If live material has moved on from the pinned acceptance data, record the discrepancy there. The verifier checks the record's structure offline but does not fetch or replay its URLs; genuine research must be visible in your tool trace and the record you produce.

`specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json` is the complete Apache-2.0 installer specification from tag `9.0.0.0` of `vmware/vcf-api-specs`, with provenance in `specifications/vcf-installer/official-source.json`. Put the deployable installer object under `greenfieldSddcSpec`. It must validate as `#/components/schemas/SddcSpec` from that exact document. Use `workflowType` `VCF_EXTEND`, create a new vCenter and dedicated NSX deployment, include all eight site-assigned hosts, omit `sddcManagerSpec`, and represent the supplied networks and distributed-switch uplinks without changing their values.

The architecture document must also contain `capacityPlan`, `availabilityPlan`, and `migrationPlan`. `capacityPlan` must use the fields `required`, `perHost`, `plannedHostCount`, `dataHostsPerSite`, `cpuOvercommitRatio`, `reservePercent`, `survivingSiteCapacity`, and `meetsSingleSiteLoss`. Show the requested capacity and per-host assumptions from the inventory; calculate the capacity remaining in either surviving data site and state whether it meets every requirement. Use integer GiB and round reserved memory down. For mirrored stretched storage, surviving usable storage is one data site's raw storage after the stated reserve. `availabilityPlan` must use `topology`, `failureRequirement`, `dataSites`, `witnessSite`, and `managementDomainChange`; each `dataSites` item uses `id` and `hosts`. Name both data sites, every host assigned to each, the witness site, the `SINGLE_SITE_LOSS` failure requirement, the `VSAN_STRETCHED_CLUSTER` topology, and `managementDomainChange` `NONE`.

`fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json` is the non-rotting grading authority for supported source/target combinations and transition order. Emit `migrationPlan` in its fixed schema: `{"schemaVersion":1,"estateId":string,"targetRelease":string,"steps":[...]}`. Each step has exactly `sequence`, `componentId`, `componentType`, `currentVersion`, `targetVersion`, `action`, and `gates`. Include every component from the estate exactly once, in the snapshot's order; preserve its current version from the inventory and take its target, action, and ordered technical gates from the snapshot. Do not mutate, upgrade, replace, or redeploy any management-domain component. The live research informs your work, but when live pages and the pinned snapshot differ, the artifact must follow the pinned snapshot so verification stays deterministic.

Do not edit `TestMain.java`, `protected/`, `fixtures/`, `specifications/`, or `.gitignore`. Acceptance is `python3 -B protected/verify.py`. It compiles the single implementation file with the protected harness, runs it with the shipped fixtures, validates `greenfieldSddcSpec` against the installer specification's own schema before performing any architecture checks, and then checks the architecture against the estate inventory and pinned compatibility snapshot plus the offline structure of `researchConsulted`. Verification never contacts a live endpoint.
